title: Independence of coordinate vector from the special coordinate
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and an index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $\mathrm{DisjointCoordinate} = \{\text{neither}, \text{leftOnly}, \text{rightOnly}\}$ be the three-element type. On the product space $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \times (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{DisjointCoordinate})$ form the product of the uniform law on the special coordinate and the uniform law on disjoint-coordinate vectors, and condition it on the event that the first coordinate equals $i$. Then under this conditional law the second coordinate is identically distributed to a uniformly random disjoint-coordinate vector.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
a fixed index i in Fin n
product of the uniform law on Fin n with the uniform law on disjoint-coordinate vectors
conditioning on the event that the first coordinate equals i
replaced: Conditioning the product law for $(T, coordinates)$ on $T=i$ leaves the second coordinate uniform.
